The first GoogleDoc is a list of reports of HCQ efficacy. Some of the entries are laughable. They include Dr. Marc Siegel (Fox's TV doc) and Dr. Oz with sample sizes of 1 and 2, respectively. They include preliminary data from Dr. Didier Raoult, but it should be noted that none of his currently published work assesses clinical outcomes. He assesses viral counts, which aren't the same thing by a long shot. The list isn't of the highest quality. The evidence is case reports or case series. None of it is matched against a control group, except the flawed VA retrospective, which is worthless because they were only giving HCQ to their sickest patients. They don't distinguish between HCQ for treatment of diagnosed disease and HCQ for prevention. No randomized controlled trial data is available. There is no evidence that the drug actually causes improvement in clinical status. To cite this document as poorly written and curated as it is smacks of laziness and makes the organization look bad.

The second GoogleDoc is a list of published studies on the topic. Again, we're dealing with poor quality evidence. One of my biggest issues with this document is that there's no effort to grade the evidence, or even highlight the type of study. It is clearly NOT being annotated by someone with a background in medical research. They cite case reports and case series. They cite uncontrolled, open-label prospectives. They cite in-vitro data.
